2016_097_071916mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of July 19, 2016, held at 5:30 p.m. in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Most of the volume is consent-agenda material: minutes of six June 2016 meetings and the Treasurer's Report for May 2016, which records total disbursements in the period of $10,790,131.46. The attached June 21, 2016 minutes carry the 2016/2017 appropriations resolution setting the General Fund at $142,948,405 and levying 18.0000 mills on non-homestead property for general operating and 4.7000 mills on all properties for debt retirement. New-teacher hires, administrative contract extensions and MHSAA membership complete the agenda.

## Cover and agenda
Troy School District Board of Education agenda for a regular meeting at 5:30 p.m. on July 19, 2016, in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000; www.troy.k12.mi.us). Meetings broadcast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and online at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Consent items A through G cover the June 7 special meeting and closed session, June 7 regular meeting, June 14 special meeting and closed session, June 14 workshop, June 21 special meeting and closed session, June 21 regular meeting, and the Treasurer's Report. Labeling conflicts appear: item B reads "July 7, 2016" against June 7 attachments, item G reads "April 2016" against a May 2016 report, and resolution number 16-054 is used three separate times.

## June 7, 2016 meetings
The special meeting convened at Athens High School at 5:30 p.m. under President Philippart with Fleming, Hauff, Miletti and Schmidt present and Edmunds and Underwood absent; Superintendent Machesky, Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris and West attended. Resolution 16-054 moved a closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) at 5:32 p.m.; adjourned 6:30 p.m. The regular meeting began at 7:00 p.m. with approximately 400 audience members. Rick L. West was honored as 2015-16 Oakland County School Business Administrator of the Year, presented by OCSBO President Tina Kostiuk, and board members read All-State athletes, Senior Scholar Athletes carrying a 3.5 cumulative GPA, and dozens of academic awards.

Actions, all Yes 7, No 0: 16-044 approved the May 3 and May 17, 2016 minutes; 16-045 ratified the tentative agreement reached May 25, 2016 with the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA for July 1, 2016 through June 30, 2017; 16-046 approved new hires Stephanie Pilarski, Michael Thomas, Alyssa Kay, Elizabeth Twentyman, Kathryn Starn and Duane Goulbourne; 16-047 appointed Dan Mills assistant principal at Athens High School and 16-048 appointed Mike Cottone principal at Troy Union Elementary School, each on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure beginning July 1, 2016; 16-049 set the public hearing on the proposed 2016-2017 budget for June 21, 2016 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, with notice at least six days beforehand carrying in 11-point bold faced type the statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied to support the proposed budget will be a subject of the hearing, and Exhibit A making copies available at the Administration Building from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. June 15 through June 21, 2016, signed by Secretary Paula Fleming; and 16-050 accepted the MASB-SEG Property/Casualty Pool proposal effective July 1, 2016, not to exceed $276,715.00. Dr. Machesky reported 112 Troy graduates at the International Academy graduation. Adjourned 9:09 p.m.

## June 14, 2016
The special meeting opened at 5:02 p.m. in the Administration Building with Schmidt absent. Resolution 16-051 awarded sidewalk and concrete replacement to Luigi Ferdinandi & Son, not to exceed the annual budgeted amount, from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund; 16-052 awarded interior painting to Paint Plus, Inc. in the amount of $65,000 inclusive of contingency, plus future work at bid hourly rates, from the 2014 Capital Maintenance Fund; both Yes 6, No 0. 16-053 moved a closed session on superintendent evaluation at 5:15 p.m.; adjourned 6:45 p.m. The board workshop followed at 6:50 p.m. with consultant Bill Bowman of Great Northern, covering the Section 1 property, the May cash position and budget report, the 2015/2016 final budget amendment and proposed 2016/2017 budget, summer learning, ELD, MHSAA eligibility and early childhood; adjourned 10:45 p.m.

## June 21, 2016
The special meeting convened at the Services Building at 5:45 p.m. with attorney Gary Collins of Collins & Blaha; closed session 5:46 p.m., adjourned 6:40 p.m. The regular meeting opened with the public hearing on the proposed 2016-2017 budget at 7:00 p.m.; Rick West presented tax values, homestead and non-homestead forecasts, the foundation allowance, the increase in student enrollment, and general fund revenues and expenditures. No audience member spoke; the hearing closed at 7:18 p.m. Approximately 60 people attended. Recognitions covered retiring School Life Troy photographer Ed Morykwas, with publisher Raad Alawan presenting a certificate; a School Year in Review video from Kerry Birmingham, Director of Communications and Strategic Initiatives; Mina Mori of the Wayne State University Center for Peace and Conflict Studies, whose "Discovering Japan in the 21st Century" program guided seven teachers and two board members for ten days in Japan, with a certificate presented by Brenda Carter, President-Elect of the Michigan Association of School Boards; fourth-year Spirit of Diversity Awards from the Troy Diversity & Inclusion Council; and Dr. Machesky's selection as a National School Public Relations Association 2016 "Superintendent to Watch," recognizing fewer than 25 superintendents nationally.

Actions: 16-054 approved the Treasurer's Report for April 2016; 16-055 approved new hires Brittany Beylerian, Julia Alder, Katherine Eve, Katherine Kolber, Laura Ferris and Lauren Brown; 16-056 extended the Superintendent's contract from July 1, 2016 through June 30, 2018 without tenure; 16-057 extended contracts through June 30, 2018 without tenure for Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning, Rick West, Assistant Superintendent Business Services, Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent Elementary Instruction, and Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent Employee Services. Christin Silagy updated the board on the ELD program, WIDA alignment and the EL Handbook.

Resolution 16-058 amended the 2015/2016 general appropriations: General Fund $142,161,937; Food Service Fund $3,182,130; Troy Career Center Fund $2,103,221; Adult Education/Community Service Fund $5,239,522; Facility Rental Fund $1,300; Debt Service Funds $16,635,088; Capital Projects Fund $19,540,000; Capital Maintenance Fund $300,000. Resolution 16-059 adopted the 2016-17 appropriations: General Fund $142,948,405; Special Revenue Funds 8,782,050; Debt Service funds 15,785,396; 2014 Capital Project Funds 10,270,000; Capital Maintenance Funds 2,469,355 — with millage rates of 18.0000 mills on Non-Homestead for general operating, 11.6320 mills on Commercial Personal Property, 5.6320 mills on Homestead, and 4.7000 mills on All Properties for debt retirement. Resolution 16-060 renewed the food service contract with Sodexo Management, Inc. for 2016/2017; 16-061 authorized ASTI to work with the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality on preservation mitigation credits for the Section 1 vacant property, charged to the Capital Maintenance Fund; 16-062 urged the Governor to veto Section 152b of the proposed School Aid Budget, which allocates $2.5 million for nonpublic schools, citing Article VIII Sec. 2 of the Michigan Constitution. All were Yes 6, No 0, Underwood absent. Mrs. Edmunds announced she would not run again and that two board seats were open in the November election. Adjourned 8:53 p.m.

## Personnel and curriculum items for July 19
Item 6.A recommends probationary contracts for the 2016-2017 school year to eight teachers at 1.0 FTE: Sabrina Stevanovic, Special Ed Reading Resource Room, Barnard Elementary; LaDonna Hunter, 5th Grade, Martell Elementary; Jennifer Erff, ASD Room, Costello Elementary; Sarah Nunez, Kindergarten, Wattles Elementary; Amanda Guibord, Biology/Chemistry, IA Okemos/IA East; Erica Conklin, ASD, Barnard Elementary; Anne Gallagher, Special Education Resource Room, Troy High School; and Christina Rick, ESL, Troy High School, with biographical sketches listing degrees from Michigan State University, Saginaw Valley State, Baker College, Clarion University, Central Michigan, Grand Valley State and Oakland University.

Item 6.B recommends extending 34 administrators' contracts through June 30, 2018, without tenure in the administrative positions and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook: principals Lara Dixon (Athens), Remo Roncone (Troy High), Joe Duda (Larson), Timothy Fulcher (Smith), Audra Melton (Baker), Joyce Brasington (Wattles), Janice Brzezinski (Hill), Brian Canfield (Schroeder), Tammy DiPonio (Costello), Sarah Glasser (Hamilton), Matt Jansen (Wass), Melanie Morey (Barnard), Erica Rolack (Leonard), Jeremy Whan (Bemis) and Stephanie Zendler (Morse); associate principal Ryan Brinks, International Academy-East; assistant principals Melissa Curth, Robert Dowd, Dan House, William Turner, Amy Buchanan, Jonathan Cross, Diane Kocenda and Anthony Morse; directors Kerry Birmingham, Rob Carson, Jennifer Gottlieb, Michael Jolly, David Pass, Christin Silagy, Stephanie Trotter and Kris Young; and supervisors Adrian Dean and John Schiesler.

Item 7.A enrolls the six secondary schools of the Troy School District, City of Troy, County of Oakland, as members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association, a voluntary nonprofit corporation, from August 1, 2016 through July 31, 2017, adopting the MHSAA Constitution and By-Laws and the current HANDBOOK as minimum standards. Item 7.B seeks MHSAA approval for a cooperative team in Boys' and Girls' Skiing with Athens High School for the 2016-17 and 2017-18 school years.
